workflow_phases.description_verbatim: We follow the literature (Bates et al., 2009; Opler et al., 1999) in our empirical testing and control for several variables that affect firm cash policy. Specifically, we control for Firm Size, Firm Age, Book Leverage, Market-to-book, Cash Flow, Capital Expenditure, Acquisition Expenditure, Dividend Paying Firms(0/1), R&D Expenditure, Net Working Capital, and Industry Cash Flow Volatility. The definitions of all the variables are detailed in the Appendix.

key_ambiguities: Software / package choice is not stated. The paper does not mention Stata, R, SAS, or any specific routine (reghdfe, areg, plm, fixest, etc.). For a multi-way FE model with state-clustered SE this is non-trivial because finite-sample corrections, default DOF adjustments, and singleton handling differ across packages.

Exact Compustat field mappings for each control variable are not stated. Table A1 uses natural-language phrasing (e.g., 'earnings after interest, dividends, and taxes but before depreciation') without restating Compustat item codes; the reader must back these out, with multiple plausible mappings for several variables (Cash Flow, Net Working Capital, Industry Cash Flow Volatility).

Order of operations between Phase 2 (sample construction) and Phase 5 (winsorization) is not stated. Winsorizing before sample filters versus after will yield slightly different 1st/99th percentile cutoffs.

Winsorization partition is not stated. The phrase 'at the 1st and 99th percentiles' is silent on whether winsorization is pooled across the full 1997-2015 panel, by year, by industry, by Fama-French 49 industry-year, or some other slice.

Missing-value handling is specified only for Dividend Paying Firms(0/1) ('set to zero if missing'). For all other controls (including R&D Expenditure and Acquisition Expenditure, which have very high Compustat missingness rates), the paper is silent on whether missing values are dropped or imputed to zero. The published N=56,646 and the >50% mass at exactly zero in Table 1 Panel A's Acquisition Expenditure quartiles strongly suggest zero-imputation, following the inherited Bates 2009 / Opler 1999 convention, but this is not stated.

AT timing on denominators is inconsistent in Table A1. Cash, Capital Expenditure, Acquisition Expenditure, and R&D Expenditure use 'at the beginning of the year' explicitly; Book Leverage, Market-to-book, Cash Flow, and Net Working Capital use 'book assets' or 'total book assets' without a timing qualifier. Whether contemporaneous or lagged AT is used in the latter group is ambiguous.

Industry Cash Flow Volatility construction rolling window is partially specified ('previous 10 years; at least 3 years of observations required') but the year-zero treatment is unclear (does year t use years t-10 to t-1, or t-9 to t, or t-9 to t including t?). This affects which firm-years are dropped at the start of the 1997-2015 window.

Headquarters-state assignment source is not stated. Compustat's STATE field is current-year HQ; some studies use historical HQ (e.g., from 10-K filings) because firms relocate. The paper does not say which.

PRC data integration sequence: 'We then manually merge the disclosed breaches with the CRSP/Compustat data' is silent on the matching procedure (firm name fuzzy-match, CIK, ticker, hand-checked?), but this only matters for Table 6+, not Table 2 Column 1.

Firm FE in Column (1): the Equation (1) display includes nu_i (firm FE), but Section 4.1 says Column (1) includes only year, industry, and state FE. The display equation appears to be a generic template applied selectively across Table 2 columns; readers must consult each column's FE-row labels to know which FE actually entered.

Heteroskedasticity-consistent vs state-clustered SE wording: Table 2 notes say BOTH 'standard errors are clustered by state' AND 'Heteroskedasticity-consistent standard errors are reported in parentheses'. The reconciliation is presumably cluster-robust (CR1) SE, but the exact estimator (Liang-Zeger, Stata cluster(state), reghdfe default, etc.) is not named.
